literal: He was transferred again to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
idiomatic: He was transferred again to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

literal: At the battle of Mang Mountain the main army fared ill; Jin led his subordinates in feigned surrender and stood on the left of the road.
idiomatic: At Mang Mountain the main force was losing; Jin led his men in a false surrender and posted them on the left side of the road.

literal: Gao Huan, pressing the victory in pursuit northward, took no precautions.
idiomatic: Gao Huan, riding the victory in pursuit, suspected nothing.

literal: Jin struck from the rear; the enemy were greatly alarmed.
idiomatic: Jin struck from behind, and the enemy panicked.

literal: Dugu Xin also gathered troops in the rear and struck fiercely; Gao Huan's army fell into disorder, and by this the main army was preserved whole.
idiomatic: Dugu Xin rallied men behind them and hit hard; Gao Huan's lines broke, and the main army escaped intact.

literal: In the twelfth year he was appointed Left Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing and concurrently Director of the Directorate of Agriculture.
idiomatic: In year twelve he became Left Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing and also Director of the Directorate of Agriculture.

literal: When Hou Jing came over in submission and asked for troops as aid, Jin remonstrated that Jing's intentions could not be gauged; Yuwen Tai would not listen.
idiomatic: When Hou Jing submitted and asked for reinforcements, Jin warned that Jing's loyalty was unknowable; Yuwen Tai would not hear it.

literal: Before long he was additionally Grand Master of Writing on the Great Pacification Commission and Chief Clerk to the Grand Chancellor, leading troops to garrison Tong Pass, further appointed Governor of Hua Province, granted one jar of black-millet ale, with jade libation vessels as the secondary gift.
idiomatic: Soon he was also Grand Master of Writing on the Great Pacification Commission and chief clerk to the Grand Chancellor, commanding troops at Tong Pass; he was made Governor of Hua, granted a jar of black-millet ale and jade libation vessels besides.

literal: Shortly he was appointed Minister of Works.
idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was made Minister of Works.

literal: In the first year of Emperor Gong of Wei he was made Governor of Yong Province.
idiomatic: In the first year of Emperor Gong of Wei he was appointed Governor of Yong.

literal: At the beginning, Emperor Yuan of Liang at Jiangling succeeded to the throne and secretly communicated with Qi, intending to invade and raid.
idiomatic: Earlier, when Emperor Yuan of Liang took the throne at Jiangling, he had secretly dealt with Qi and planned an incursion.

literal: His elder brother's son, the Prince of Yueyang Cha, was then Governor of Yong; because Emperor Yuan had killed his elder brother Yu, a breach opened between them, and Cha seized Xiangyang and came over in submission.
idiomatic: His nephew Cha, Prince of Yueyang, held Yong; when Yuan killed Cha's brother Yu, the rift was beyond repair—Cha seized Xiangyang and defected.

literal: Jin was then ordered to march out against him.
idiomatic: Jin was ordered to march against him.

literal: Yuwen Tai saw him off at Qingni Valley.
idiomatic: Yuwen Tai saw him off at Qingni Valley.

literal: Changsun Jian said: "What plan will you make for Xiao Yi?"
idiomatic: Changsun Jian asked, "What plan will you make for Xiao Yi?"

literal: Jin said: "Display troops on the Han and Mian, sweep across and cross the Yangtze, seize Danyang directly—that is the upper stratagem."
idiomatic: Jin said, "Mass troops on the Han and Mian, sweep down the Yangtze, and seize Danyang—that is the best plan."

literal: Move the people within the outer walls into the inner city and hold the inner city awaiting relief—that is the middle stratagem.
idiomatic: Evacuate the outer city into the inner citadel and wait for aid—that is the middling plan."

literal: If moving is difficult and one holds the outer ramparts—that is the lower stratagem."
idiomatic: If he cannot bear to move and merely holds the outer walls—that is the worst plan."

literal: Jian said: "Which stratagem will Yi adopt?"
idiomatic: Jian said, "Which will Yi choose?"

literal: Jin said: "He will certainly use the lower."
idiomatic: Jin said, "The worst—certainly."

literal: Jian said: "Why?"
idiomatic: Jian asked, "Why?"

literal: He replied: "The House of Xiao has held the south for generations spanning several reigns."
idiomatic: He replied, "The Xiao have held the south for generations."

literal: Just when the central plains had troubles, they had no leisure for outward campaigns.
idiomatic: While the central plains were in turmoil they had no leisure to look outward.

literal: Moreover, because we have the trouble of Qi, he is sure to think our strength cannot be divided.
idiomatic: And seeing our trouble with Qi, he will assume we cannot spare a force.

literal: Moreover Yi is timid and without stratagem, suspicious and slow to decide.
idiomatic: Yi himself is timid, unstrategic, suspicious, and slow to decide.

literal: Fools are hard to plan with from the start; all cling to their towns and dwellings, detest removal, and will hold the outer ramparts.
idiomatic: Common men hate upheaval; they will cling to their homes, dread moving, and defend the outer walls.

literal: Therefore he will use the lower stratagem."
idiomatic: So he will take the worst plan."

literal: Jin ordered the Duke of Zhongshan Hu and the great general Yang Zhong and others first to seize Jiangjin and cut off his escape routes.
idiomatic: Jin sent the Duke of Zhongshan Hu and the great general Yang Zhong to seize Jiangjin first and cut off retreat.

literal: The men of Liang erected wooden palisades on the outer city, sixty li in circumference.
idiomatic: The Liang raised wooden palisades around the outer city, sixty li around.

literal: Before long Jin arrived and invested it with his full force.
idiomatic: Soon Jin arrived and invested the place with his full strength.

literal: After sixteen days the outer city fell; the Liang ruler withdrew to hold the inner city.
idiomatic: In sixteen days the outer city fell; the Liang ruler withdrew into the inner citadel.

literal: The next day he led his heir apparent and the rest, bound themselves with ropes before Jin, and surrendered.
idiomatic: The next day he led the crown prince and his court out, bound in ropes, and surrendered.

literal: Shortly he was put to death.
idiomatic: Soon afterward he was executed.

literal: He captured men and women numbering more than a hundred thousand and seized the treasures of the palace storehouses.
idiomatic: They took more than a hundred thousand captives and seized the palace treasuries.

literal: They obtained the armillary sphere of Song, the Liang sundial, the bronze gnomon, Wei's wind-indicating bird, the bronze coiled-dragon pedestal, a great jade disk seven feet across and seven feet in circumference, and various chariots and ritual objects, which were presented up; the army took nothing for itself.
idiomatic: They took Song's armillary sphere, the Liang sundial, bronze instruments, Wei's wind-vane bird, a coiled-dragon bronze pedestal, a great jade disk seven feet across, and chariots and ritual gear—all sent up; the army kept nothing private.

literal: Cha was installed as ruler of Liang; the army shook out its banners and returned.
idiomatic: Cha was installed as Liang ruler; the army withdrew in good order.

literal: Yuwen Tai personally came to his residence; their banquet talk was exceedingly merry.
idiomatic: Yuwen Tai came in person to his house; their feast ran to great merriment.

literal: Jin was rewarded with a thousand male and female slaves.
idiomatic: Jin was rewarded with a thousand slaves.

literal: Together with Liang treasures, there was also one set of metal, stone, silk, and bamboo music, and he was separately enfeoffed as Duke of Xinye.
idiomatic: With Liang treasures came a full court orchestra; he was separately enfeoffed Duke of Xinye.

literal: Jin firmly declined; he was not permitted.
idiomatic: Jin firmly declined; it was not allowed.

literal: He also had the Music Office compose ten songs, "The Duke of Changshan Pacifies Liang," and had artisans sing them.
idiomatic: The Music Office was ordered to compose ten songs, "The Duke of Changshan Pacifies Liang," for artisans to sing.

literal: Jin, considering himself long in heavy authority with merit already established, wished to preserve ease and leisure, and so presented up the fine horses he had formerly ridden and the armor he had worn.
idiomatic: Jin, long in power with his fame made, wished for ease and returned the fine horses and armor he had used.

literal: Yuwen Tai understood his intent and said: "The great villain is not yet pacified—how can you alone seek your own good so soon?"
idiomatic: Yuwen Tai read his intent and said, "The great foe is not yet down—can you seek comfort alone?"

literal: He therefore did not accept them.
idiomatic: He would not accept them.

literal: When the Six Offices were established, Jin was appointed Grand Minister of Justice.
idiomatic: When the Six Offices were established, he became Grand Minister of Justice.

literal: When Yuwen Tai died, Emperor Xiaomin was still young; the Duke of Zhongshan Hu, though entrusted in the testament, had always ranked below the others, and each duke plotted to seize power.
idiomatic: When Yuwen Tai died, Emperor Xiaomin was still a child; Hu of Zhongshan, though named in the will, had always ranked low, and every duke plotted for power.

literal: Hu was deeply worried and secretly consulted Jin.
idiomatic: Hu was deeply worried and sought Jin in secret.

literal: Jin said: "Having long received the Chancellor's special favor, today I will dispute it to the death."
idiomatic: Jin said, "I have long owed the Chancellor; today I will dispute this to the death."

literal: "If the policy is settled before the assembly, you certainly cannot yield."
idiomatic: "Settle it before the assembly, and you cannot be refused."

literal: The next day the dukes met in council.
idiomatic: The next day the dukes met.

literal: Jin said: "In former days the imperial house was tottering; the Chancellor's will was to rescue and restore."
idiomatic: Jin said, "When the house was falling, the Chancellor meant to set it right."

literal: "Now Heaven sends calamity and suddenly abandons the hundred officials."
idiomatic: "Heaven has sent calamity and taken him from the hundred officials."

literal: "The heir, though young, is yet the Duke of Zhongshan, close kin like a son, and also entrusted in the testament—military and state affairs ought by right to fall to him."
idiomatic: "The heir is young, but Hu of Zhongshan is kin like a son and named in the will—state and army belong to him."

literal: His words were stern and forceful; all were shaken.
idiomatic: His tone was fierce; everyone flinched.

literal: Hu said: "This is a family matter—how dare Hu decline!"
idiomatic: Hu said, "This is family business—how dare I refuse!"

literal: Jin having been treated as an equal by Yuwen Tai and the rest, Hu always showed him ritual respect.
idiomatic: Jin had stood as Yuwen Tai's equal; Hu always treated him with ceremony.

literal: At this Jin rose and said: "If you take charge of army and state, we shall have someone to rely on."
idiomatic: Now Jin rose and said, "Take army and state, and we have someone to follow."

literal: He then bowed twice.
idiomatic: He bowed twice.

literal: The dukes, pressed by Jin, also bowed.
idiomatic: Pressed by Jin, the dukes bowed as well.

literal: The assembly's decision was then settled.
idiomatic: The matter was settled.

literal: When Xiaomin ascended the throne, Jin was advanced to Duke of Yan with a fief of ten thousand households, transferred to Grand Tutor and Grand Director of the Ancestral Temple, and with Li Bi and Hou Mo Chen Chong and others deliberated on court affairs.
idiomatic: When Xiaomin took the throne, Jin was made Duke of Yan, fief of ten thousand households, Grand Tutor and Grand Director of the Ancestral Temple, and deliberated policy with Li Bi and Hou Mo Chen Chong.

literal: When Helan Xiang campaigned against Tuyuhun, Emperor Ming ordered Jin to command his army from afar and gave him strategy.
idiomatic: When Helan Xiang marched on Tuyuhun, Emperor Ming had Jin direct the army from afar and gave him the strategy.

literal: In the second year of Baoding, Jin because of age asked to retire; an excellent edict would not permit it.
idiomatic: In Baoding year two, Jin asked to retire on account of age; a gracious edict refused.

literal: In the third year he was made one of the Three Elders; he firmly declined and was again not permitted.
idiomatic: In year three he was made one of the Three Elders; he declined again and was refused again.

literal: He was granted the staff of longevity.
idiomatic: He was granted the staff of longevity.

literal: Emperor Wu visited the Imperial Academy to feed him.
idiomatic: Emperor Wu came to the Imperial Academy to serve him.

literal: When the Three Elders entered the gate, the emperor met and bowed to him beyond the screen; the Three Elders returned the bow.
idiomatic: As the Three Elders entered, the emperor met and bowed beyond the screen; the Elder bowed in return.

literal: The officials set the Three Elders' mat at the central pillar, facing south.
idiomatic: Officials set the Elder's mat at the central pillar, facing south.

literal: The Grand Preceptor, Duke of Jin Hu, ascended the steps, set the mat and placed the armrest.
idiomatic: The Grand Preceptor, Duke of Jin Hu, mounted the steps and set mat and armrest.

literal: The Three Elders ascended the mat, sat facing south leaning on the armrest, placing himself in the teacher's position.
idiomatic: The Elder took the mat, faced south, leaned on the armrest, and held the teacher's place.

literal: The Grand Minister of Justice, Duke of Chu Ning, ascended the steps and straightened his shoes.
idiomatic: The Grand Minister of Justice, Duke of Chu Ning, mounted the steps and straightened his shoes.

literal: The emperor ascended and stood before the axe-screen, facing west.
idiomatic: The emperor mounted and stood before the axe-screen, facing west.

literal: The officials brought food; the emperor knelt to set out sauce and beans and personally bared his arm to cut the meat.
idiomatic: Food was brought; the emperor knelt to set sauce and beans and cut the meat himself.

literal: When the Three Elders had finished eating,
idiomatic: When the Elder had finished eating,

literal: the emperor again knelt in person to present the cup for rinsing the mouth.
idiomatic: the emperor knelt again and offered the rinsing cup.

literal: The officials withdrew the vessels.
idiomatic: The vessels were cleared away.

literal: The emperor stood facing north to inquire about the Way.
idiomatic: The emperor stood facing north to ask about the Way.

literal: The Three Elders then rose and stood at the mat.
idiomatic: The Elder rose and stood at his mat.

literal: The emperor said: "I rashly bear the realm's heavy burden; considering myself without talent, I do not know the essentials of governance—please instruct me."
idiomatic: The emperor said, "I bear the realm's weight unworthily and do not know governance—teach me."

literal: The Three Elders answered: "Wood follows the line and becomes straight; a lord who follows remonstrance becomes sage."
idiomatic: The Elder answered, "Wood follows the line and grows straight; a ruler who hears remonstrance becomes sage."

literal: "From antiquity enlightened kings and sage lords have all received remonstrance with an open mind to know gain and loss, and the realm was thereby secure."
idiomatic: "Sage kings of old all welcomed honest counsel to know their errors, and the realm was secure."

literal: "May Your Majesty keep this in mind."
idiomatic: "May Your Majesty remember this."

literal: He also said: "The root of governing a state lies in loyalty and trust."
idiomatic: He also said, "The root of statecraft is loyalty and trust."

literal: "The ancients would give up food or arms, but trust could not be lost."
idiomatic: "The ancients would give up food or arms, but never trust."

literal: "The rise and fall of states have never been without this—may Your Majesty hold to it and not lose it."
idiomatic: "States rise and fall by this—hold it and do not let it go."

literal: He also said: "The way to govern a state must have law."
idiomatic: He also said, "To govern there must be law."

literal: "Law is the state's cord and net and cannot fail to be set right."
idiomatic: "Law is the state's net—it must be straight."

literal: "What must be set right lies in reward and punishment."
idiomatic: "What must be straight is reward and punishment."

literal: "If there is merit, reward; if there is crime, punish—then those who do good daily increase and those who do evil daily cease."
idiomatic: "Reward merit and punish crime, and good grows while evil stops."

literal: "If there is merit and no reward, crime and no punishment, then good and evil in the realm are not distinguished and inferiors have nowhere to place hand or foot."
idiomatic: "Without reward or punishment, good and evil blur and men have nowhere to stand."

literal: He also said: "Words and conduct are the foundation of establishing the person; words go forth and conduct follows—sincerely may Your Majesty be cautious."
idiomatic: He also said, "Word and deed are a man's foundation—deeds follow words; be cautious, Majesty."

literal: When the Three Elders had finished speaking, the emperor bowed twice to receive it; the Three Elders returned the bow; the rites were completed and they withdrew.
idiomatic: When the Elder had finished, the emperor bowed twice to receive the teaching; the Elder bowed in return; the rites ended and they withdrew.

literal: When the Duke of Jin Hu campaigned eastward, Jin was then ill.
idiomatic: When Duke of Jin Hu marched east, Jin was ill.

literal: Hu, because he was an old general and veteran minister, still asked him to go together and consulted him on military strategy.
idiomatic: Hu, honoring an old commander, still asked him along and sought his counsel on strategy.

literal: When the army returned, he was granted one set of bells and chimes.
idiomatic: On the army's return he was given bells and chimes.

literal: In the second year of Tianhe he was again granted one cushioned carriage.
idiomatic: In Tianhe year two he was again granted a cushioned carriage.

literal: Shortly he was appointed Governor of Yong.
idiomatic: Soon he was made Governor of Yong.

literal: In the third year he died, aged seventy-six.
idiomatic: In year three he died, aged seventy-six.

literal: The emperor came in person.
idiomatic: The emperor came in person.

literal: An edict ordered Prince of Qiao Jian to supervise the funeral rites, granted a thousand bolts of silk and a thousand hu of grain, posthumously conferred his former offices, further made him Bearer of the Staff with full credentials, Grand Preceptor, Commander-in-Chief over twenty provinces including Yong and Heng, Governor of Yong, posthumous title Wen.
idiomatic: Prince of Qiao Jian was ordered to oversee the funeral; a thousand bolts of silk and a thousand hu of grain were granted; his offices were posthumously confirmed, with Bearer of the Staff, Grand Preceptor, command over twenty provinces including Yong and Heng, Governor of Yong, posthumous title Wen.
